newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares off on Dadas bankruptcy talk.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares off on Dadas bankruptcy talk.

text.p: Slovenian shares fell 2.56 percent on Wednesday, knocked down by a newspaper report that brokerage Dadas may face bankruptcy if a merger with Primofin is blocked by its shareholders at a meeting later this month.
The 10-share SBI index fell 30.67 points to 1,165.6 on turnover of 264.1 million tolars, down from 533.9 million on Tuesday. Two stocks rose, 17 fell and five were untraded.
Shares in Dadas tumbled 13.50 percent or 1,620 tolars to end at 10,380 tolars, making them by far the session's biggest decliner. Volume stood at of 515 shares.
Slovenian daily Finance said Dadas' management feared the firm would go under if shareholders voted against the merger with brokerage Primofin at the November 29 meeting.
No-one at Dadas was available for comment.
Traders said uncertainty surrounding the makeup of the new government was also weighing on prices.
Final unofficial election results from Sunday's general election show that the ruling centre-left Liberal Democrats may have to relinquish power to the rightwing "Spring" alliance.

"Foreign investors are standing back a bit and watching what happens but companies in Slovenia are still attractive and rated well," said Fritz Schweiger, head of equity research at Investmentbank Austria in Vienna.
Bank SKB was the most actively traded share, falling 4.52 percent to 42,010 tolars on volume of 2,363 shares for total turnover of 100,9 million tolars
Bank Vipa was the biggest gainer, firming 2.44 percent to 42,000 tolars on volume of 18 shares for total turnover of 756,000 tolars. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
